text: Hercules is a Romano-Celtic god. Celtic artists did not usually show gods in human form. The invading Romans arrived around 200 BCE. The Celts then adapted their style to classical figure modeling. The Interpretatio Romana renamed Celtic gods with Roman names. This practice encouraged artists to carve gods with classical and Celtic features. They labeled the gods with Roman names. The Greco-Roman hero Hercules appears often in Celtic art. He appears especially on the Continent. He stands as an altered version of Celtic gods. Some of those gods still have known names. Others do not. Segomo, Borvo, and Smertrius all appear as brawny gods. They carry Herculean clubs. What these gods meant to their people is unclear. Borvo links to the healing springs at Aix-les-Bains. He may have fought disease, not other gods. The second-century Greek writer Lucian said the god of eloquence, Ogmios, was shown as Hercules. Verbal talent was a kind of strength for the Celtic people.
